One synthetic quarter, read three ways. Switch views with the tabs or the arrow keys, or link straight to one with `#tab=sales`.

## Overview {#overview}

The example closes September at **$630K MRR**, up **61.5% from July's $390K**. Enterprise supplied $140K of the $240K increase; mid-market supplied the remaining $100K.

```metric
value: 630000
label: Q3 ending MRR
format: number_compact
unit: $
delta: 0.6153846154
delta_label: vs July
trend: up
```

```callout
kind: neutral
title: Three coordinated views
body: |
  Overview sets the frame, Sales breaks the lift down by segment and Customers shows the ending book of business. Each view has its own link, such as `#tab=customers`, and its charts keep their state when you switch away and back.
```

## Sales {#sales}

Enterprise MRR rose from $280K to $420K; mid-market rose from $110K to $210K. The rows establish those changes. They contain no customer, sales-cycle or intervention data, so they do not establish why the increases happened.

```chart
type: bar
title: MRR by segment, Q3
subtitle: Enterprise contributed 58.3% of the $240K increase from July to September
data:
  inline:
    - { month: Jul, mrr: 280000, segment: enterprise }
    - { month: Jul, mrr: 110000, segment: mid-market }
    - { month: Aug, mrr: 340000, segment: enterprise }
    - { month: Aug, mrr: 160000, segment: mid-market }
    - { month: Sep, mrr: 420000, segment: enterprise }
    - { month: Sep, mrr: 210000, segment: mid-market }
encoding:
  x: month
  y: mrr
  color: segment
axes:
  y: { label: MRR, format: number, unit: $ }
annotations:
  - { kind: point, at: { x: Aug, y: 340000 }, text: Enterprise reached $340K }
  - { kind: point, at: { x: Sep, y: 420000 }, text: Enterprise reached $420K }
style:
  ratio: "16:9"
```

| Segment    | July MRR | September MRR | Growth  |
|---         |---:      |---:           |---:     |
| Enterprise | $280K    | $420K         | +50%    |
| Mid-market | $110K    | $210K         | +90.9%  |
| Total      | $390K    | $630K         | +61.5%  |

## Customers {#customers}

The ending book of business shifted toward enterprise accounts. The chart counts distinct customers paying in September; it does not establish retention or churn.

```chart
type: pie
title: September customers by segment
subtitle: Enterprise accounts made up 44% of the ending book
data:
  inline:
    - { segment: Enterprise, customers: 22 }
    - { segment: Mid-market, customers: 28 }
encoding:
  x: segment
  y: customers
style:
  ratio: "1:1"
```

```callout
kind: hold
title: No causal conclusion from these rows
body: |
  These synthetic monthly rows contain no pricing or retention evidence. Check real source data and distinguish recurring revenue from one-time effects before using a similar report for planning.
```

## Verification

Run `richview check` for source and chart-geometry diagnostics, then inspect each view at its intended desktop and phone widths. A printout or PDF shows all three views in order, and readers without JavaScript see them stacked. These checks do not certify the analysis.
